summary: Identity propagation delay prevents dashboard session token refresh for internal analytics console
description:
Issue summary:
Users intermittently see a 401/403 from the internal analytics dashboard (console) immediately after an Okta profile change or a forced session refresh. The auth flow fails during the token refresh step: the auth-proxy exchanges the refresh token but the returned ID token appears to contain stale group/role claims, which the console then rejects due to tightened RBAC checks deployed last week.

Impact:
- ~12 engineers reported inability to load analytics dashboards since 2026-03-10 09:00 UTC.
- Affects internal dashboards and tooling only (not customer-facing APIs).
- Productivity hit for dashboard users and oncall when trying to verify incidents.

Environment:
- prod - us-east cluster serving internal-console routes.
- Okta as IdP, auth-proxy (v1.8.3) sits between console and Okta.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Log into console with a session established earlier (long-lived).
2) From Okta admin, update user's group membership (add/remove from analytics-admin).
3) Trigger console session refresh (browser refresh or wait for automatic refresh).
4) Observe 403 with "insufficient_role_claims" or 401 with "token_mismatch" in logs.

Expected behavior:
- After Okta claim change, the next refresh should either pick up new claims or gracefully fall back to previous session until the user reauths.

Actual behavior:
- Race condition: auth-proxy serves an ID token which appears to be from an older claim snapshot while backend RBAC service has the updated state, resulting in immediate denial.

Logs / evidence:
- auth-proxy logs (excerpt): "INFO exchange_refresh_token: returned id_token issued_at=1616161616 claims_version=42; cache_version=41"
- console logs: "ERROR access_check: claim_version_mismatch user=priya.shah@redwood.ai required=42 provided=41"
- Okta system log shows successful group update at 2026-03-10T09:02:14Z for affected users.

Business impact:
- Internal only, but P1 because it impedes oncall incident verification and slows engineering work.

Workarounds observed:
- Manual sign-out + full reauth resolves the issue for users.
- A temporary mitigation is to revert the strict claim_version enforcement in RBAC service (risky; requires rollback and careful rollout).
investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: identity cache/claim snapshot used by auth-proxy is behind Okta event processing or the token exchange pipeline; caching layer (claim-cache) may be serving stale claim bundles during refresh windows.

What we checked so far:
- Verified Okta event shows groups updated before auth-proxy token exchange.
- Replayed token exchange in staging: auth-proxy returns id_token with claims_version from local claim-cache, which is updated asynchronously by a background worker.
- Background worker shows occasional processing lag when claim updates are frequent (observed timestamps gap of up to 90s under burst).

Hypothesis: claim-cache update is eventual and not coordinated with token issuance; when RBAC service enforces claim_version strictly, short windows cause 403s.

Next steps:
- Add a short TTL invalidation on claim-cache on Okta webhooks (owner: auth-proxy team).
- Add defensive logic in RBAC service to accept id_token if issued_at is within 2m of claim update OR prompt reauth rather than 403.
- Add metrics and an alert for claim_version_mismatch rate > 1/min.
- Schedule a patch release for auth-proxy (v1.8.4) to synchronously refresh claims on token-exchange when webhook events are present.

Owners assigned: auth-proxy (Liam), RBAC (Sofia Martinez), SRE (Carlos Vega).
comments: 2026-03-10 10:12 - Support (Priya Shah): Created ticket after oncall reported that several engineers could not access the analytics dashboards following an Okta group change. Attached initial logs and user repro steps.

2026-03-10 13:05 - Liam O'Connor (auth-proxy): Confirmed we return id_tokens with claims_version equal to the claim-cache snapshot. Background worker lagged; suspect race with Okta webhook processing. Adding higher priority to this.

2026-03-11 09:20 - Sofia Martinez (RBAC): RBAC service started enforcing claim_version strictly after last week's rollout. Suggest degrade enforcement to tolerate a 2-minute drift until fix is deployed.

2026-03-12 15:34 - Carlos Vega (SRE): Observed spikes in claim-cache processing time correlated with batch webhook delivery. Created temporary alert and increased worker concurrency; saw reduction in mismatch events in canary.
2026-03-13 08:45 - Support (Priya Shah): Communicated manual sign-out + reauth workaround to affected users. Tracking impacted users for postmortem.

2026-03-14 11:10 - Liam O'Connor (auth-proxy): Draft PR opened to invalidate claim-cache on webhook receipt and to fetch fresh claims synchronously on token-exchange when webhook timestamp < 60s. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/auth-proxy/pull/342
resolution: (in progress) Mitigation steps applied to canary: increased claim-cache worker concurrency and temporarily relaxed claim_version enforcement in RBAC for 2-minute drift. PR for auth-proxy cache invalidation submitted. Full rollout planned once PR passes tests and security review. Will follow up with post-incident notes and longer-term plan for end-to-end identity propagation guarantees.
follow_up_actions: Deploy auth-proxy v1.8.4 with cache invalidation and sync fetch on token-exchange
Add incident runbook entry for claim_version_mismatch
Create alert for mismatch rate and Okta webhook processing lag metric
Review RBAC strictness and release guardrail for claim drift tolerance
